rationale:
ROUND 2. Round 1 was REVISE on a gating objection from editquality, plus MEDIUM objections from tooling_provenance, debug_historian, bug_historian and prior_art_librarian. Three of those changed the file; one changed the argument; one I am answering with an enumeration I should have done first. Taking them in the order they matter.

1. GATING (editquality, HIGH) -- "the sketch's UPDATE substitutes a placeholder marker, not the real prompt text". The objection was RIGHT and it was my submission that was defective, not the file: the shipped migration always carried the real dollar-quoted text (which is why the round trip measured 2766->5046), but I had replaced it in the sketch with `<<<the anchor sentence, then the block below>>>` and relegated the real text to trailing SQL comments. A reviewer could not tell a documentation shorthand from a migration that would insert a literal placeholder into the live prompt. FIXED STRUCTURALLY rather than by retyping: the sketch below is now the actual file, sliced from `BEGIN;` to `COMMIT;`, so sketch and artefact cannot diverge. That also answers debug_historian's LOW objection about no visible BEGIN/COMMIT -- the whole transaction is now in view.

2. PROVENANCE (tooling_provenance MEDIUM, debug_historian MEDIUM -- two seats, same defect). "Mutates agent_definitions.default_config with no snapshot_agent() call ... a byte-swap rollback file is not equivalent to a queryable pre-image row." Correct, and it is now fixed. The migration calls `PERFORM snapshot_agent('tool-generator', '749_...: pre-update')` inside the pre-guard, positioned AFTER the idempotency RETURN so a re-run does not mint a pointless snapshot. I verified the mechanism rather than trusting the seats' description of it: snapshot_agent copies the live row into a SEPARATE table, agent_definitions_backup (not agent_definitions with is_snapshot=true -- my first count queried the wrong table and read 0, which I chased rather than glossed). Measured in the rolled-back transaction: backup rows for tool-generator 0 -> apply -> 1 -> apply again -> STILL 1, and the pre-image reads back at length 2766, exactly the original prompt. So there is now a queryable recovery point independent of the _ROLLBACK file.

3. CONTAINMENT (prior_art_librarian, MEDIUM). "The 'Tier 2 cannot dispatch tool-improver' claim checks only evaluateStaticCriteria; a landmine says component_level='tool' opts into check_tool_health -> tool-improver, a route not gated by no_auto_fix." This is the "an objection naming one file is naming a CATEGORY" lesson and I had earned it by checking one function and generalising. The claim SURVIVES, but only now that it is enumerated. Every producer of an improve_tool work item, from grep over platform/ and internal/:
   (a) discovery_checks/check_tool_acceptance.go:274 -- Tier 2. READS the fence; its criteria switch has no computed_values arm so the type falls to `default: skip(...)`. Its three built-in shell checks run "always ... independent of the criteria" (:94), so they are unaffected by fence content.
   (b) discovery_checks/check_tool_health.go:308 -- DOES raise improve_tool and does NOT honour no_auto_fix, exactly as the objection says. But it CANNOT be affected by this change: grep for 'criteria|doc_plans|Criteria' over that file returns ZERO hits. It never reads a fence, so adding a check type to one changes nothing it sees.
   (c) refresh_evidence_fact_drift.go:415 -- READS the fence (tool.Criteria) and DOES honour no_auto_fix, routing to fact_drift_review instead (:52-57).
   (d) tool_acceptance_actions.go -- Tier 4. Honours no_auto_fix: ":38 A fence carrying top-level no_auto_fix: true never reaches tool-improver at all."
   (e) core-manager/admin/confirm_work_item_handler.go:98 -- human-initiated follow-up, not automatic.
   So: of the five, the three that read a fence either skip computed_values or honour no_auto_fix; the two that do not read a fence cannot be moved by fence content. Exposure widens by zero rows -- now by enumeration, not by one grep.

4. THE UNENFORCEABLE TRUST BOUNDARY (bug_historian, MEDIUM). "The refusal arm is prose in a prompt with no code-side check that the asserted value is independently derivable ... it can make the failure less likely, not detect it." I accept this entirely and I am not going to pretend a prompt closes it. Two things I have done rather than argue: (i) the prompt now separates the two acts that were previously blurred -- DERIVE THE VALUE FROM THE RULE; READ THE FORMAT OFF THE CODE -- because the honest path was previously unavailable (a model that could not predict the rendered format had to either refuse or read the whole value off the page, and the second is the failure you name); (ii) the detector this wants is recorded as a follow-on candidate rather than hand-waved: a check comparing a newly authored expect_values against what the tool itself renders, flagging the case where they match while ## Dependencies names no rule and shows no working. That is mechanically checkable and it is the enforcement point. It is deliberately NOT in this migration, because it is a new detector with its own footprint and belongs in its own round.

5. PEER-LANE CONTRIBUTION FOLDED IN. Between rounds, the loancalculator_couk lane (owner of toolgolden.py, asked 2026-09-03) answered in bugs_open/449 sections A-C. Two of its findings changed the prompt text in this round:
   (i) "An input vector is PART OF THE EXPECTATION'S IDENTITY." Their bug 385 established that stored and composed bytes are different name-spaces on exactly this pipeline; the generator reads draft markup while the checker drives the deployed artefact. The prompt now says WRITE THE INPUTS AS LITERAL VALUES -- never "the page default", never a reference the checker resolves later.
   (ii) The format/locale point: fill "300000" and the page displays "300,000". Since comparison collapses whitespace and is otherwise exact, a correct derivation can fail on presentation. Hence the value/format split in (4)(i).
   Their third finding -- that between reactivity and pinned values there is a middle rung of RELATIONAL assertions (monotonicity, sign, bounds), derivable from a tool's purpose with no known-good state -- is a genuinely better answer for the tools this migration teaches to REFUSE, and would catch the 0%-APR-computes-nothing class that reactivity passes. It needs a new check type in the runner, so it is filed as a follow-on, not smuggled in here.

6. NOT CHANGED, and why. (a) prior_art_librarian LOW: the motivating counts live in doc_plans, which that seat cannot query. I cannot fix the seat's schema access; the exact query is in bugs_open/449 section 9e and the lane's RUNBOOK section 1b so it is reproducible by anyone who can reach the table. (b) prior_art_librarian LOW on duplicate active rows: already covered -- the pre-guard aborts unless the anchor count is EXACTLY 1, so two active rows abort rather than half-apply; the seat's own read-only check returned count 1. (c) guardian LOW on bundling two changes: kept bundled deliberately, and the pre-guard requires both or neither, because shipping the vocabulary without the budget is the worse half-applied state. (d) llm_reliability LOW on adaptive thinking competing with max_tokens: noted; a truncated PLAN costs a missed check, not a corrupted verdict.

RE-TESTED AFTER EVERY CHANGE ABOVE, in a rolled-back transaction against the live row: 2766 -> apply -> 6013 -> apply again (UPDATE 0, "already applied", post-verify still passes) -> reverse -> 2766, byte-identical to baseline. The _ROLLBACK file is REGENERATED from this migration by script (the header carries the three lines that do it) so its literals are byte-identical by construction; the first cut was hand-written with a regexp, failed on a newline and a dropped apostrophe, and reported UPDATE 1 while substituting nothing -- caught only by the post-verify DO block, which is the argument for writing verifies that RAISE.

PATHS MENTIONED HERE THAT ARE NOT IN THE EDIT LIST: docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/749_..._ROLLBACK.sql (companion, regenerated and round-trip tested, but _ROLLBACK is out of council scope as it is not the change); check_tool_health.go, check_tool_acceptance.go, refresh_evidence_fact_drift.go, tool_acceptance_actions.go, confirm_work_item_handler.go, run_checks_action.go (READ as evidence for the enumeration in (3), none modified); bugs_open/449 and the lane's working docs (prose, out of scope). No Go file is touched by this submission.

plan.summary: ROUND 2 of bugs_open/449 candidates 1+2. Migration 749 teaches tool-generator's compose_plan prompt the computed_values check type AND when to refuse to write one. Changes since round 1: (a) the sketch is now the literal file from BEGIN; to COMMIT; so sketch and artefact cannot diverge — the gating objection; (b) snapshot_agent('tool-generator') is called in the pre-guard, after the idempotency return, giving a queryable pre-image (verified 0->1->1, pre-image length 2766) — raised by two seats; (c) the containment claim is now an ENUMERATION of all five improve_tool producers rather than one grep; (d) the prompt gains two rules from the loancalculator lane: literal input vectors, and derive-the-value-but-read-the-format.

edits.rationale: New migration, round 2. Pre-guard: counts each verbatim anchor, RAISE EXCEPTION unless exactly 1 (which also covers the duplicate-active-row case a seat asked about), early-RETURN if already applied, then snapshot_agent() for a queryable pre-image. Two surgical replaces: the criteria vocabulary gains computed_values with a default-REFUSAL arm, and the document cap moves 3000->3600 characters so the new check is not traded against prose. Post-verify is a DO block that RAISES on seven conditions including the absence of the refusal arm, so the capability cannot ship without its brake. The sketch below is the file itself from BEGIN; to COMMIT;, verbatim, so what is reviewed is what applies. Companion 749_..._ROLLBACK.sql is regenerated from this file by script (byte-identical literals by construction) and round-trip tested, but is out of council scope as it is not the change.

This second path is not checked or ruled out anywhere in the submission.'

Verified answer to that objection: grep for 'criteria|doc_plans|Criteria' over platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/check_tool_health.go returns ZERO hits — it never reads a fence, so fence content cannot move it.
platform/orchestration/actions/tool_acceptance_actions.go:38 — 'A fence carrying top-level no_auto_fix: true never reaches tool-improver at all: a failing verdict goes straight to the [human]'.

Measured in a rolled-back transaction 2026-09-03: agent_definitions_backup rows for tool-generator with snapshot_reason LIKE '749%' went 0 -> 1 after the first apply -> STILL 1 after a second apply, and the stored pre-image reads length 2766, exactly the pre-change prompt.
Round-2 round trip, rolled back: 2766 -> apply -> 6013 -> re-apply (UPDATE 0, 'already applied' NOTICE, post-verify passes) -> reverse -> 2766.

The fence carries the input vector VERBATIM, as literal values — never the page default, never a reference the checker resolves later', citing their bug 385 that stored and composed bytes are different name-spaces on this pipeline.

loancalculator_couk lane, bugs_open/449 section B2: 'the checker asserts-then-drives those exact values and reads the control back after driving (format/locale rewriting: fill 300000, the page displays 300,000)'.

plan.risks:
WHAT A REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK IN ROUND 2, in the order I think it matters.

1. THE TRUST BOUNDARY IS STILL NOT CLOSED, AND I HAVE NOT CLAIMED IT IS. bug_historian's round-1 objection stands on its own terms: a prompt cannot detect a model that convinces itself a heuristic score is a "published formula". What changed is that the honest path is now reachable (the value/format split means a model no longer has to read the page to get the format right), and that the enforcement point is named as a follow-on detector rather than left implicit. If a seat believes the capability should not ship at all until that detector exists, that is a coherent position and I would rather hear it now -- my counter is that the refusal branch is the default, so the expected outcome for most tools is today's PLAN plus one Dependencies line, and that shipping the vocabulary is what makes the detector's input population exist at all.

2. IS THE VALUE/FORMAT SPLIT SOUND, OR DOES IT REOPEN THE DOOR IT CLOSES? I now tell the model to read the rendering FORMAT off the tool's own code while deriving the VALUE independently. I believe these are genuinely separable -- the format is a presentation fact about the code, the value is an arithmetic fact about the world -- but it does licence the model to look at the code for one purpose while forbidding it for another, and that is a fine line to walk in a prompt. If a reviewer thinks this is too subtle to hold, the alternative is to require a looser assertion (interaction/text_matches on a pattern) whenever the format cannot be derived, which is weaker but unambiguous.

3. THE SNAPSHOT IS NEW THIS ROUND AND IS ITSELF UNTESTED IN ANGER. snapshot_agent() fires and writes a readable pre-image (verified: 0->1->1, pre-image length 2766). What I have NOT done is exercise a restore FROM that backup row; I am relying on the estate's convention that agent_definitions_backup is the recovery path. If the restore direction has its own trap, this migration inherits it, and the _ROLLBACK file remains the tested reversal.

4. BLAST RADIUS IS UNCHANGED FROM ROUND 1 and is every tool built from now on. Config, live on apply, no image to roll back. Containment: additive to a prompt whose existing instructions are untouched; default is refusal; Tier 2 skips the type; no_auto_fix taught defensively; and now a queryable pre-image exists before the write.

5. DEFERRED, STILL: experience-planner (3 fences, 3 anchors), the 55 component-subject fences (bugs_open/449 section 9f), backfill of the 55 driving-and-blind tool fences (where bugs_open/441's stale-selector risk actually bites), and the relational-assertion rung the loancalculator lane proposed (needs a new runner check type). The architecture seat's round-1 note is worth repeating to whoever picks these up: if a THIRD producer needs this vocabulary, that repetition is the signal to build a shared prompt fragment rather than re-anchor per-agent text a third time.
